about.title: Lynwood Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Long Beach Boulevard runs the length of Lynwood, and the I-105 Glenn Anderson Freeway cuts straight through the city. Add Imperial Highway and Atlantic Avenue, and you have four corridors where a large share of the city's reported collisions occur. In 2025, Lynwood recorded 304 injury crashes, leaving 398 people hurt and three families grieving. Public records show reports peak on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m., when the afternoon commute is heaviest. If one of those crashes was yours, the days after can feel disorganized. Doctors, body shops, and an adjuster who calls before you have finished your first round of appointments. LawProactive exists to make one part of that simpler. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Lynwood residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims across Los Angeles County. There is no charge to be matched, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you owe no fee unless there is a recovery. You focus on healing; a professional handles the paperwork and the phone calls.

whyChoose.title: Why Lynwood Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: The clock is real, and it can be short
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but a claim involving a city vehicle, a Caltrans stretch of Imperial Highway, or another public agency may need to be filed within six months. An attorney can tell you which deadline applies before it slips by.

items.title: Partial blame does not erase your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover even if you were partly responsible, with your share reduced by your percentage of fault. The other insurer knows this and may push you to accept more blame than the facts support.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, so there is nothing to pay up front and nothing owed if the case does not result in compensation. Being connected through LawProactive costs you nothing at any stage.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are generally not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company, and it is usually wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions in ways that can later be used to shift fault or minimize your injuries. A simple, polite refusal is enough.

items.question: I was hit near the I-105 on-ramp at Long Beach Boulevard. What should I save?
items.answer: Photos of both vehicles, the ramp, lane markings, and any debris are worth keeping, along with the CHP or Sheriff's report number if one was taken. Save the names of witnesses, your medical paperwork, and any texts or voicemails from insurers. Freeway and ramp footage from nearby businesses or agencies may be overwritten quickly, so an attorney will often request it early.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering in California?
items.answer: For ordinary car accident cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages such as pain, emotional distress, and loss of enjoyment of life. The amount depends on the specific facts, the severity of your injuries, and how well the evidence is documented. No attorney can promise a particular result, but a thorough case gives you a fair chance at full compensation.
